title: New Mutual Aid Network Launched
intro: In East Charlotte, a new mutual aid center has opened to help neighbors get support faster.
The center focuses on food, basic supplies, and creating a place where people feel welcome asking for help.
body: ## What the center provides
The center provides pantry food, hygiene items, and everyday supplies that many families rely on. Volunteers greet visitors and help them find what they need for the day.
Because the location is close to several apartment communities, residents can walk in without needing transportation. This makes help easier to reach during busy or stressful times.
The space is calm and welcoming, allowing people to slow down and feel comfortable. Visitors are encouraged to ask questions and learn about resources nearby.
## Support beyond supplies
Volunteers take time to listen and offer guidance. They help explain what support is available and how to access it.
For people who need additional help, the center shares information about food pantries, benefits assistance, and housing services in the area.
## How the community can help
Community members support the center by donating unopened items or helping during sorting and packing days. Even a small amount of time makes a difference.
The network is built on trust and care. It aims to strengthen relationships between neighbors and reduce feelings of isolation.
The long term goal is to help people meet immediate needs while also connecting them to ongoing support across the community.

title: Upcoming Job Fair
intro: A job fair in Uptown is bringing employers and training programs together in one place.
It gives job seekers a chance to explore opportunities and learn what companies are looking for.
body: ## What you will find there
Visitors can meet hiring teams and learn about open roles across different industries. Employers are ready to answer questions and share details about their work.
Many companies talk about schedules, expectations, and opportunities for growth. This helps visitors understand what daily work might look like.
## Preparing to show up strong
Bringing a resume can be helpful, but it is not required. The event is designed to welcome people at different stages of their job search.
Some tables offer guidance for resumes and interviews. These tips can help job seekers feel more prepared and confident.
Talking with employers in person allows visitors to make a stronger impression. A short conversation can help build a connection.
## After the event
The location is accessible and close to public transportation. This makes the event easier to attend for many residents.
Job seekers are encouraged to take notes and collect contact information. This can be useful after the event ends.
Following up with employers by applying online or sending a message can help keep the conversation going.

title: Free Wellness Clinic Weekend
intro: A free wellness clinic weekend in West Charlotte will offer basic health screenings and support.
The clinic welcomes families and seniors who want to learn more about their health.
body: ## What the clinic offers
Staff and volunteers provide basic checkups and screenings during the event. They explain results and suggest next steps when needed.
The clinic is designed to feel friendly and low stress. Visitors are encouraged to ask questions and take their time.
Information about local clinics and community health programs is also available. This helps visitors find affordable care options.
## Help for people without regular care
People without insurance are welcome to attend. Staff share information about low cost services and support programs.
Bringing identification or a list of medications can be helpful, but it is not required. The focus is on making care accessible.
## Tips for a smoother visit
Arriving earlier in the day may help reduce wait times. Staff aim to give each visitor enough attention.
Families can also ask about routine care for children and older adults. The clinic helps plan future visits.
The goal is to help people feel informed and supported when making health decisions.

title: New Rent Assistance Intake Dates
intro: New intake dates are available for residents seeking rent assistance in North Charlotte.
These programs help families stay housed during challenging financial times.
body: ## Getting ready to apply
Many assistance programs ask for basic documents such as identification, proof of income, and lease information. Preparing these ahead of time can help.
Some programs also request notices related to rent balance or payment history. Checking requirements early can reduce stress.
## What happens at intake
During intake events, staff often explain eligibility and guide applicants through the process. This support helps people understand each step.
If one program is not a match, staff may suggest other options. Many groups also connect residents to food and utility support.
## Staying on track
Arriving early can increase the chance of being seen. Intake spots may be limited on busy days.
Bringing copies of documents can be helpful so originals stay safe. Staff can explain what happens after applying.
Residents who miss an intake date are encouraged to watch for future sessions. Staying informed is important.
These programs aim to provide stability and reduce the risk of eviction for families in need.

title: After School STEM Signups Open
intro: After school STEM programs are now open for students who enjoy hands on learning.
These programs help students grow skills while building curiosity and confidence.
body: ## Learning through projects
Students take part in activities that focus on learning by doing. Projects allow them to test ideas and see results.
Programs often include coding, robotics, engineering builds, and science activities. These experiences connect school lessons to real world skills.
## Building confidence and teamwork
Working in groups helps students practice teamwork and communication. They learn how to share ideas and solve problems together.
The environment encourages creativity and exploration. Making mistakes is part of the learning process.
For families, these programs offer a safe place for students after the school day ends. This can make daily schedules easier.
## How to join
Some programs include time for homework or tutoring before activities begin. This supports academic success.
Meeting schedules vary depending on the program. Families can choose what fits best.
Early registration is recommended since space may be limited. Waitlists are often available.

title: Volunteer Drives This Saturday
intro: Citywide volunteer events this Saturday invite residents to support local efforts.
Activities include food packing, cleanup projects, and donation sorting.
body: ## Easy to join
Most volunteer roles are beginner friendly and open to all experience levels. Instructions are given at the start.
Volunteers may help pack food boxes, organize supplies, or clean shared spaces. Each task supports the community.
## A good way to connect
These events are a good way to meet others and learn about local organizations. Many people return after their first experience.
Some locations allow volunteers to choose tasks based on interests. Options include indoor and outdoor work.
## Making the day go smoothly
Shifts run for several hours, but flexible attendance is often allowed. Even a short visit is helpful.
Comfortable clothing and closed shoes are recommended. Organizers aim to keep tasks safe and simple.
Attending with friends can make the experience more enjoyable. Group signups may be available.
Volunteering helps strengthen neighborhoods and builds a sense of shared responsibility.
